- If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and forecast is above recent lows, reduce forecast by 1–2% to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after sharp price spikes; cap upward revisions to 10% of prior peak to prevent overshoot.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is trending, apply mean reversion bias: forecast next period as 0.95×previous + 0.05×current if no strong signal.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, reweight toward recent 7-day trend unless sentiment overrides.  
- If sentiment history shows consistent 0.00 and forecast is erratic, apply smoothing: average last 3 forecasts before adjusting.  
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes should be corrected by 15–20% reduction in next period if no new data confirms continuation.
